newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela backs down on jaguar hunt proposal.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela backs down on jaguar hunt proposal.

text.p: Venezuela, under fierce attack from conservationist groups, said on Monday it had decided against allowing hunters to shoot rare jaguars to raise funds to protect the species.
"After carefully studying the proposal ... the Environment Ministry has decided ... not to allow the limited jaguar hunt," the ministry said in a statement.
Under the plan, hunters were to be charged up to $12,000 per head for killing about 30 of the big cats per year.
But conservationists labeled the hunt "barbaric" and said it would not help protect the roughly 3,600 jaguars left in Venezuela.
